intro: Country duets from two voices that know each other well.
story: Caleb Klauder was raised on Orcas Island and helped found Foghorn Stringband; Reeb Willms joined him in Portland, and together they lead a country scene there. Innocent Road, on West Sound in 2016, was followed by NPR Music's pick of "There Goes My Love" in its Songs We Love. They came back to Pickathon in 2018, and Gold in Your Pocket came out on Free Dirt on November 15, 2024.
artist_reel_line: Gold in Your Pocket came out on Free Dirt on November 15, 2024.

intro: Ukrainian folk polyphony, in tall hats, from Kyiv.
story: DakhaBrakha formed in Kyiv in 2004 at the Dakh Contemporary Arts Center, as a theater music project of the director Vladyslav Troitskyi, and they call their sound ethno-chaos. They played NPR's Tiny Desk in April 2015, globalFEST in 2014 and a KEXP session on April 23, 2017. They came to Pickathon in 2018. Ukraine awarded them the Shevchenko National Prize in 2020, and in April 2022 they toured the U.S. weeks after Russia's invasion; NPR reported the band calls itself an ambassador of free Ukraine. Ptakh, in 2025, was their first studio album in five years.

intro: A Swedish songwriter of raw, wooded folk-blues.
story: Daniel Norgren was born on July 18, 1983, and raised outside Borås, Sweden, and has released music on the small Superpuma label since 2006; his debut, Kerosene Dreams, was mostly made on homemade instruments. He played Pickathon in 2016 and again in 2018. Wooh Dang, his first widely distributed album, came out on April 19, 2019, with a US release through Yep Roc. He recorded it live to analog tape in a 19th-century farmhouse, and NPR's First Listen and Rolling Stone both reviewed it.
artist_reel_line: Wooh Dang was recorded live to analog tape in a 19th-century farmhouse.

intro: A DIY punk band with a new record.
story: Dopey's Robe is a DIY punk band that had newly signed with a booking agent when it came to Pickathon in 2018. Its self-titled album, Fasting for the Ceiling, came out in April of that year, and an earlier LP was called Who and When Is Stephen Networks? Gigwise filmed the band in a Pickathon Pumphouse session.
artist_reel_line: Fasting for the Ceiling came out in April 2018.

intro: A supergroup of songwriters, with one record.
story: Glorietta is an Austin supergroup of Matthew Logan Vasquez, David Ramirez, Kelsey Wilson, Noah Gundersen, Adrian Quesada and Jason Robert Blum. Its first show was at Newport Folk in 2018, and the self-titled debut came out that August. Glide named Glorietta among eight acts that blew them away at Pickathon 2018. The four front members have since gone back to their own records.

intro: Arabic-language hardcore punk from New York.
story: Haram is a New York hardcore band that sings entirely in Arabic; the name means forbidden. Their full-length When You Have Won, You Have Lost came out in 2017 on Toxic State, and they played Pickathon in 2018. The EP Where Were You on 9/11? followed in April 2019. A new album, Why Does Paradise Begin in Hell, came in fall 2025, and Treble listed Haram among that fall's essential punk albums.

intro: An Appalachian duo working in drone and old ballad.
story: House and Land is an Asheville, North Carolina, duo of Sarah Louise Henson and Sally Anne Morgan of the Black Twig Pickers, who met when Henson opened for Morgan's band. Their self-titled debut came out on Thrill Jockey in June 2017, and Magnet ranked it the number 25 album of 2017. They played Pickathon in 2018. Across the Field followed on Thrill Jockey in June 2019, and Bandcamp Daily ran a feature on it.

intro: A touring folk songwriter with a funny, loose stage presence.
story: John Craigie was born on June 15, 1980, and raised in Los Angeles; he studied at UC Santa Cruz and fronted the psychedelic band Pond Rock before going solo, and moved to Portland around 2015. No Rain, No Rose, from 2017, was recorded at home in Southeast Portland with guests including the Shook Twins and Gregory Alan Isakov, and Jack Johnson championed his live album Capricorn in Retrograde. Scarecrow came out in May 2018, the year of his Pickathon set. Mermaid Salt followed in 2022 and Pagan Church in 2024 on his own Zabriskie Point label, and I Swam Here in 2026.

intro: A songwriter of soft, shuffling indie-folk.
story: Michael Nau spent the better part of a decade in the indie pop duo Cotton Jones, in Cumberland, Maryland, before going solo. Mowing, his solo debut, came out on February 19, 2016, made of unused material from those years, and Some Twist followed on June 16, 2017. Michael Nau & The Mighty Thread came out in 2018, the year he played Pickathon. Accompany, his fifth solo album, arrived on December 8, 2023, and Glide called it his best solo effort to date.

intro: A Tucson big band of cumbia, mambo and psychedelic rock.
story: Sergio Mendoza, born in Nogales, founded Orkesta Mendoza in Tucson in 2009 as a one-off tribute to the Cuban mambo king Pérez Prado that was too much fun to stop. Mambo Mexicano came out in 2012, La Rienda in 2014, when they played WOMEX, and ¡Vamos A Guarachar! in 2016. La Caminadora, from 2018, was the year of their Pickathon set. Curandero, on Glitterbeat in 2020, earned a Songlines Best Group nomination in 2021.
artist_reel_line: Curandero, on Glitterbeat in 2020, was nominated for a Songlines award.

intro: A Texas baritone with an outlaw-country swagger.
story: Paul Cauthen was born in Tyler, in East Texas, to a religious family, and began in a duo with David Beck while living in San Marcos. My Gospel came out in 2016 and was number 23 on Rolling Stone's top 40 country records of that year. The Have Mercy EP, recorded live in Dallas with the Texas Gentlemen, came out on June 22, 2018, and he played Pickathon that summer. He lived almost two years in Room 41 of Dallas's Belmont Hotel after a breakup and wrote the next record there; Room 41 came out on September 6, 2019. Country Coming Down followed on Thirty Tigers in 2022, and Book of Paul in 2026.

intro: A North Carolina multi-instrumentalist and roots collaborator.
story: Phil Cook was born in Wisconsin and is based in North Carolina. He co-founded Megafaun with his brother Brad and the drummer Joe Westerlund, played earlier in DeYarmond Edison with Justin Vernon and in Gayngs, and has played on records by Hiss Golden Messenger and the Blind Boys of Alabama. Southland Mission, his solo debut, came out on September 11, 2015, co-produced with Brad. He played Pickathon in 2018, and All These Years followed in 2021 and Appalachia Borealis in 2025.
artist_reel_line: Southland Mission, his solo debut, was co-produced with his brother Brad.

intro: Matthew Houck's indie-folk project.
story: Matthew Houck, from Huntsville, Alabama, began recording as Phosphorescent in 2001 in Athens, Georgia. Muchacho, on Dead Oceans in March 2013, appeared on more than a dozen year-end lists. C'est La Vie, his first album in five years, came out in 2018, the year he played Pickathon; by then he had moved to Nashville, built a studio and had two children. Revelator, in 2024, was his first album for Verve, about home, partnership and family.

intro: A Portland rapper from the city's underground scene.
story: Rasheed Jamal was born in Hot Springs, Arkansas, and moved to Portland in 2008, where he formed the Resistance crew with Mic Capes and Glenn Waco. Willamette Week called him a rising figure in Portland hip-hop and a teacher-philosopher among the city's rappers. He played Pickathon in 2018, and SANKOFA has been his most recent focus.

intro: A New York blues-rock band fronted by Kia Warren.
story: Revel in Dimes is a New York blues-rock band fronted by Kia Warren. They released the single "Kissing" in the spring of 2018 and played Pickathon that summer, where Flood Magazine heard fire in their set and they were paired with the chef Han Ly Hwang for the Friday Curation dinner.

intro: Sisters Leah and Chloe Smith, in global folk harmony.
story: Leah Song and Chloe Smith were raised in Atlanta by a fiddler mother and a sculptor father, and recorded their first album, Leah and Chloe, in a friend's basement studio in 2005. After a 2014 tour of Scotland they decided to slow down and stay, and they run the Slow Music Movement as a way of rooted touring. Alive, a live album, came out on September 28, 2017, and they played Pickathon in 2018. Leylines followed in 2019, Folk & Anchor in 2024 and then Trade My Troubles.

intro: A Seattle songwriter, a familiar voice in Northwest folk.
story: Sera Cahoone was raised near Deer Creek Canyon in Littleton, Colorado, and moved to Seattle in 1998, where she played with Carissa's Wierd and Band of Horses. Signed to Sub Pop in 2007, she released Only as the Day Is Long in 2008 and Deer Creek Canyon on September 25, 2012, produced with Thom Monahan. With Jason Kardong she was the first to play on the Space Needle roof, for Sub Pop's Silver Jubilee in July 2013. Baker Lake came out in March 2018 on her own label, Lady Muleskinner, after she left Sub Pop, and she played Pickathon that summer. I've Missed You All These Years came out on Sub Pop in 2026.

intro: Kevin Russell's horn-fueled Austin soul band.
story: Shinyribs began in 2007 as a solo side project of Kevin Russell of the Gourds, and became his main band when the Gourds went on hiatus in 2013. The Austin Chronicle said the second album, Gulf Coast Museum, deserved to drop the term side project. In 2017 they won Funk/Blues/Soul Band of the Year at the Austin Music Awards and placed second for Best Austin Band. I Got Your Medicine came out that year, and they played Pickathon for a fourth time in 2018. Transit Damage followed in 2023.

intro: Ryan Gustafson's North Carolina indie-folk project.
story: The Dead Tongues is the project of Ryan Gustafson, a North Carolina songwriter who has also played guitar with Hiss Golden Messenger and Phil Cook. Unsung Passage came out in 2018, the year of the Pickathon set, and Transmigration Blues followed in 2020; Gustafson said it is about little deaths and rebirths, and trying to find a place of purpose and compassion. Dust came in 2022, and in June 2024 two albums, Body of Light and I Am a Cloud, came out on Psychic Hotline.

intro: A Los Angeles rock band built around Natalie Carol's voice.
story: Valley Queen formed in Los Angeles in 2014 around Natalie Carol, who grew up in Little Rock, Arkansas; they started as college friends with the bassist Neil Wogensen and changed names around 2015. Supergiant came out on Roll Call on July 13, 2018, produced by Lewis Pesacov, and Rolling Stone heard a mountain-vaulting dream-country yodel. They played Pickathon that summer. Chord of Sympathy followed in 2023, and Carol has since played solo shows in the Southwest.

intro: A Los Angeles psych band, then an orchestral-minded one.
story: Wand formed in Los Angeles in 2013 around Cory Hanson, who had played with Mikal Cronin, PANGEA and Meatbodies, and Ty Segall handpicked them for his God? label on Drag City. Ganglion Reef came out in 2014, Golem and 1000 Days in 2015 and Plum in 2017. The Perfume EP followed on May 25, 2018, the year of their second Pickathon, and Laughing Matter in 2019. Vertigo, on Drag City on July 26, 2024, was Stereogum's Album of the Week, which called Wand among the most underrated rock bands working.
artist_reel_line: Vertigo came out on Drag City on July 26, 2024.

intro: An Austin indie-pop band, soft and chamber-folk-minded.
story: Wild Child formed in Austin in 2010 around Kelsey Wilson and Alexander Beggins, who met as backing musicians for a Danish act. Pillow Talk came out in 2011, The Runaround in 2013 and Fools, on Dualtone, in 2015, and Relix compared one track to the Supremes gone country. Expectations followed on Dualtone in 2018, and Wilson was also in Glorietta on that summer's Pickathon bill. End of the World came in 2023.

intro: A New York honky-tonk traditionalist.
story: Zephaniah OHora is a New Hampshire native based in Brooklyn, who booked the country bar Skinny Dennis in 2013 and sang for the Honeyfingers before fronting the 18 Wheelers. His debut, This Highway, came out in 2017, and Saving Country Music called it classic country mastery, while No Depression said there is nothing new in it, as high praise. He played Pickathon in 2018. Listening to the Music followed on Last Roundup Records in 2020.
